quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter the road or driveway ahead from your current direction. Turn around and find a different route.

questions.question: You are driving when it begins to rain. You should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When it rains, reduce your speed and turn on your headlights. If rain makes it hard to see, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: A driver approaching a flashing red traffic signal must:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding, not paying attention, and tailgating are major causes of crashes. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: While driving, your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go off the road, gently apply the brakes to slow down. When you reach a safe speed, gradually turn the wheel to get back on the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.
Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when you see a flagger, stop sign, gates, or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires slide on water between the tire and road. Low air pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
Do not follow specific rules of the road.
Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Treat cyclists with respect and follow the same rules.

questions.question: Fines for moving traffic violations in school zones are:
questions.explanation: In Florida, fines double for violations in school zones. You may also pay up to $1,000 in civil penalties and be required to take a driving course.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit on hills. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction to drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show them they are wrong.
Do something to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get away from an aggressive driver. Trying to get even with them makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the road.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry, you should:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them. Don't make eye contact or use hand gestures. Slow down and move away to stay safe.

questions.question: To make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them feel better?
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person get over the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal three to five seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Make sure the path is clear of traffic and pedestrians before you turn.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must show:
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must have all three documents with you when driving.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn if you miss your exit. Continue driving and use the next exit instead.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your turn or exit, you should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Continue driving until you find a safe place to turn around at the next exit or turn.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you find a safe place to turn around at the next exit or turn.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs warn of sharp curves. The arrow shows which direction the road curves. You may see several of these signs along the curve.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is ahead. Watch for trains.

questions.question: If your tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Release the accelerator slowly to reduce speed. Once you are going slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus where vehicles cannot be seen.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus where vehicles cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Vehicles in these blind spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than drinking alcohol alone.
It does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs can affect how your brain works and make it harder to drive safely. Mixing alcohol with drugs increases your risk of crashing.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make the effects of both stronger. For example, drinking one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: How should you merge into a crowded freeway?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the ramp to match the speed of the freeway traffic.
Yield to cars already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure there is room to merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not hit the brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, release the gas and do not brake right away. Slow down gradually before applying the brakes gently and pulling to the side of the road.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation.
Only looks at the car ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for things in your car, reading, looking at sights, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at your instrument panel often. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: Driving ability can be hurt by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all hurt your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use half a lane.
Share the same lane when passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give the rider a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room for both, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: When a traffic light is broken, drivers should:

options.text: Treat it like a four-way stop.
Drive through without stopping but be careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light is broken, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. The driver who gets to the intersection first has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, ignoring the guard.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if no children were around.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What should you do to stay safe when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Pass quickly under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look in both directions for trains before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep more distance between your car and the car ahead.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to drive safely in the dark for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted on the road?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles that are already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle while driving?

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply in this direction.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply in this direction.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road ahead has a sharp turn. Slow down before you reach it, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles with flashing lights and sirens. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. You must stop and yield the right-of-way. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on.
questions.explanation: At night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. This makes sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.
